title: Tight adaptive CCA frontier for multi-round TEM
summary: Determine whether every multi-round tweakable Even--Mansour construction in the source family reaches the conjectured round-dependent adaptive CCA exponent.

formal_statement.body: For every fixed integer $r>2$, prove that $\operatorname{TEM}[n,r,H]$ with independent public random permutations and independently keyed uniform $\varepsilon$-AXU masks has adaptive bidirectional CCA security up to approximately $2^{rn/(r+1)}$ queries, or give a compatible attack that refutes this frontier for some $r$.

scope.domain: Multi-round tweakable Even--Mansour ciphers in the random-permutation model under adaptive CCA.
assumptions: $H$ is uniform and $\varepsilon$-AXU, with $\varepsilon\approx2^{-n}$ for the displayed exponent.
Round permutations and hash-function keys are independent.
Construction and inner-permutation queries are adaptive and bidirectional.
scope.unresolved_remainder: No matching adaptive CCA security and attack bounds at exponent $rn/(r+1)$ are known for every fixed $r>2$.

citations.label: Cogliati--Lampe--Seurin, Tweaking Even-Mansour Ciphers
citations.locator: Introduction and Related Work and Perspectives, printed pp. 5 and 7

progress.summary: The source conjectures the $rn/(r+1)$ adaptive CCA exponent for every fixed TEM round count greater than two.
